answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by requiring each identity to lock a refundable stake that is slashed after proven misbehavior, instead of allowing free accounts. Like marble cut only after sustained work, a pearl formed slowly layer by layer, and an opal valued for a verifiable history, reputation should accrue only through completed, checkable tasks over time. An operator running many fake agents must pay the stake and time cost for every copy, while honest agents keep deposits and gain priority, so flooding the network becomes linearly expensive and unprofitable.
